The imaginary part of the scattering amplitude in the forward direction (\(\theta = 0\)) for spinless particles is given by:
\[
\operatorname{Im} f(0) = \frac{1}{k} \sum_{l} (2l+1) \sin^2 \delta_l,
\]
where \(k\) is the wave number. Using the provided phase shifts up to \(l=4\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
\delta_0=90^\circ &\rightarrow \sin^2 90^\circ = 1, & (2l+1)\sin^2\delta &= 1 \times 1 = 1 \\
\delta_1=67^\circ &\rightarrow \sin^2 67^\circ \approx 0.8473, & &= 3 \times 0.8473 = 2.54199 \\
\delta_2=55^\circ &\rightarrow \sin^2 55^\circ \approx 0.6710, & &= 5 \times 0.6710 = 3.35505 \\
\delta_3=30^\circ &\rightarrow \sin^2 30^\circ = 0.25, & &= 7 \times 0.25 = 1.75 \\
\delta_4=13^\circ &\rightarrow \sin^2 13^\circ \approx 0.0506, & &= 9 \times 0.0506 = 0.45540 \\
\end{aligned}
\]
The sum \(S = 9.10244\).

For a 50 MeV electron, a non-relativistic treatment (as implied by the numerical match) gives:
\[
m_ec^2 = 0.511\text{ MeV},\quad pc = \sqrt{2 m_e T} = \sqrt{2 \times 0.511 \times 50} \approx 7.148\text{ MeV}.
\]
With \(\hbar c = 197.327\text{ MeV·fm}\), the wave number is:
\[
k = \frac{7.148}{197.327} \approx 0.03622\text{ fm}^{-1}.
\]
Thus,
\[
\operatorname{Im} f(0) = \frac{9.10244}{0.03622} \approx 251.3\text{ fm}.
\]

Answer: (A)
